---
title: "Field Sampling"
---

The structural dataset behind this site (`Placencia_mangroves_2025.xlsx`) is collected by hand in the field, tree by tree, across three lagoon sectors — **upper**, **lower**, and **main creek** — plus a handful of offshore caye sites not yet shown on the [Sector Explorer](explorer.qmd) map.

## Data source

Field data are maintained in [Placencia_mangroves_2025.xlsx](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/14LuCtodKnOIlNhZ7m3mE5Six7Qu6T-Sr/edit?usp=sharing) on Google Drive. A local copy is fetched automatically before each site build; you can also [download the spreadsheet directly](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/14LuCtodKnOIlNhZ7m3mE5Six7Qu6T-Sr/export?format=xlsx).

## What's recorded per tree

For each sampled tree, the dataset records:

- **Location**: a station id and, for the first tree at each station, latitude/longitude.
- **Species** and **morphotype** (fringe vs. scrub growth form).
- **Trunk diameter (DBH)** and **height**.
- **Lagoon position**: upper/lower/main creek sector, and east/west bank.
- **Aboveground and belowground biomass per tree**, calculated from the measurements above.

Trees are grouped by station, with a `quarternumber` and `dist` (distance) field indicating multiple trees measured outward from each station's reference point — consistent with a transect- or quadrant-based sampling design radiating from fixed field stations.

## Methodology

The specific field protocol (plot/transect layout, DBH measurement height, biomass allometric equations used, sampling dates, and personnel) is maintained by the field team and not yet written up here. **This section is a placeholder** — if you're on the field team, replace it with the actual methodology, or open an issue/PR against the [source repository](https://github.com/USF-IMaRS/mangrove-structure-in-placencia).
